ABSTRACT
Cloud computing enables dynamic resource access, but efficient resource allocation remains challenging due to interference and
performance limitations in virtual machine (VM) management. Efficient resource allocation in cloud computing is crucial for min-
imizing interference and optimizing virtual machine (VM) performance. This study proposes a Self-Guided Quantum Generative
Adversarial Network with Prairie Dog Optimization Algorithm (SGQGAN-PDOA) to reallocate tasks across VMs dynamically.
The framework integrates Inception Transformer (IT) for feature extraction and Spatial Distribution–Principal Component Anal-
ysis (SD-PCA) for feature reduction, enhancing processing efficiency. Implemented in Java with CloudSim, the proposed model
improves resource utilization, achieving 80% reliability for 150 VMs with a 200 ms processing time. Experimental results demon-
strate significant reductions in waiting time, response time, and load imbalance, outperforming existing methods. By leveraging
quantum generative modeling and optimization, this approach enhances scalability, energy efficiency, and system responsiveness
in dynamic cloud environments. The findings suggest that quantum-inspired scheduling frameworks offer a promising solution
for adaptive and high-performance resource management in cloud computing.

Introduction
Cloud computing (CC) is a broadly adopted pay-per-use
paradigm that enforces access to computational resources
and data, as well as applications and services, by offering
internet-based data centers (DCs) [1]. These are the differentia-
tions from traditional computers, which retain data and install
software in DCs, with access to the facilities at any desired
time and space [2]. The three types of service models, namely

Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS),
and Software as a Service (SaaS), demand that service providers
have resource management and allocation to their best abilities
to fulfill the expectations of the users [3]. Resource allocation
(RA) is one of the most critical steps in achieving optimization of
resource usage, reducing costs, and maintaining agreed service
level agreements (SLAs) [4]. The static RA approaches often
result in inefficient consolidation and increased operational
costs because they fail to adapt to fluctuating workloads [5].

In contrast, dynamic RA allows the reallocation of resources
based on real-time system load, improving scalability, load
balancing, and performance [6]. However, the dynamic reallo-
cation of resources through the shutdown and restart of virtual
machines (VMs) often means that the flexibility benefit gained is
instead implemented in terms of overhead [7] (Appendix A).
One of the major concerns in DCs is power consump-
tion, especially by servers and computational resources [8].
Optimization-based strategies are designed to maintain energy
usage, which in itself will not hinder SLAs [9]. Virtualization
is inevitable in dynamic RA as it offers remapping of resources
dynamically and provides flexibility for VMs in dealing with
dynamic needs [10]. The challenges that arise from this kind
of scenario are the heterogeneous physical machine capacities,
load balancing, and preventing VM overloading, which require
advanced techniques of optimization [11, 12]. Modern dynamic
methods of RA should be aimed at effectively distributing loads
among VMs, searching for optimal configurations, and minimiz-
ing waiting time, making the resources scalable [13]. These meth-
ods are based on more complex algorithms for better resource
usage, priority balancing, and satisfying user demands with
minimal costs and performance loss [14, 15]. All these chal-
lenges of dynamic RA help ensure a strong and efficient CC
environment to handle the increasing demand for computa-
tional resources. The major contributions of this work are given
below.
• This paper proposes a conceptual model and a workable
method for achieving dynamic resource allocation by trans-
ferring requests or tasks between VMs.
• Several users send task requests to the feature extraction pro-
cedure first. During feature extraction, the Inception Trans-
former (IT) is used to extract features from the users’ tasks
and the cloud server.
• The spatial distribution-p-principal component analysis
(SD-PCA) technique is then used to lower both fea-
tures to shorten the processing time for dynamic resource
allocation.
• Moreover, both features and resource allocation are done
using the Self-Guided Quantum Generative Adversar-
ial Network with Prairie dog optimization algorithm
(SGQGAN-PDOA). The optimized work has since been
scheduled for resource assignment to a particular VM.
The rest of the research paper is organized as follows: Section 2
reviews the prevailing methodologies in the flow of method,
advantages, and demerits with the problem statement and moti-
vation; Section 3 broadly describes the proposed solution for the
stated problems; Section 4 validates the efficiency of the proposed
solution in comparison with the existing models; and finally ends
with the conclusion in Section 5.

Literature Survey
2.1
|
Description of a Few Recent Publications
on Resource Allocation in Cloud Computing
Chen et al. [16] introduced an innovative approach to resource
allocation (RA) for cloud-based software applications, utiliz-
ing workload-time Windows (DRAW) and Deep Reinforcement
learning. The DRAW model predicts proper management actions
under various system conditions, creating an objective RA plan
with a forecast accuracy of up to 90.69%. The DRAW method
outperforms other traditional approaches by 3%–13% in certain
cases.
Mangalampalli et al. [17] employed a Deep Q-learning network
method to find the best resource for a specified schedule. The
Cloudsim toolbox was used to run complex simulations, with
two stages to the process. For simulation, a randomly gener-
ated workload is first employed, followed by the effectiveness
of the presented algorithm being validated using HPC2N and
NASA workload. Baseline algorithms such as FCFS, RR, and Ear-
liest Deadline-first approaches are contrasted with DRLBTSA,
which shows improved energy usage and minimized SLA viola-
tion percentage.
Al-Wesabi et al. [18] presented novel hybrid metaheuristics for
the CCC environment’s energy efficiency resource allocation
(HMEERA). The model first carries out feature extraction pro-
cedures following task requests from numerous clients, then the
principal component analysis is used for the feature reduction
procedure (PCA). The HMEERA approach takes advantage of
integrated features, resulting in GTOA-RSO, which enhances the
cloud data center’s resource distribution across VMs.
Thakur and Goraya [19] presented a PPSO-DA approach for RA in
CC settings, reducing load imbalance between physically active
devices. The hybrid optimization technique, PPSO-DA, is based
on the dragonfly algorithm and phasor particle swarm optimiza-
tion. Simulation trials conducted with the CloudSim simulator
demonstrate that PPSO-DA dominates alternative methods.
Fathalla et al. [20] presented an innovative heuristic called the
Best K-First-Fit (Best-KFF) algorithm, finding the first k pre-
emption options at each physical machine (PM) and arranging
them according to goals like resource efficiency. The algorithm
makes the optimal decision to preserve the functionality of the
cloud computing system, reducing requirement waiting times,
lease preemption, preemption times, and energy usage.
Ullah and Nawi [21] suggested hybridizing the artificial bee
colony algorithm with the Bat algorithm (HBAC) to enhance the
load balancing method. The proposed HBAC algorithm demon-
strated a lower makespan of VMs in a cloud data center and an
increased accuracy rate in work distribution.
Zhou et al. [22] introduced GGA-HLSA-RW (GHW), a unique
family of genetic algorithms intended to maximize energy and
cloud usage. They built a Growable Genetic Algorithm employing
HLSA and random multi-weights (RW) as the growth route and

Motivation
The increasing adoption of cloud infrastructures necessitates
efficient resource utilization in cloud computing. Poor resource
management can lead to hardware underutilization, higher
operating costs, energy waste, and decreased performance.
To achieve cost-effective operations and customer satisfac-
tion, cloud providers can optimize resource allocation. A new
approach, the self-guided quantum generative adversarial net-
work (SG-QGAN), integrates quantum computing and atten-
tion refinement techniques for optimal resource allocation. This
method eliminates noise and intraclass discrepancies, enabling
effective modeling of complex resource demand patterns. This
integration sets a new benchmark for resource management
effectiveness in dynamic environments.

Proposed Methodology
Pay-as-you-use services using cloud computing can allocate
resources in a dynamic, flexible, and efficient manner. With
cloud computing, however, resource optimization is a significant
difficulty because several users can request various services at
once. In this research, a conceptual model and technique for
dynamic resource allocation through task or request migration
into VMs are proposed. The online streaming data of users or
consumers is the first thing the system receives and is retrieved
via the task manager. Next, data about job cost, speed, weight,
and size is taken out of the cloud server using the IT. The pro-
cessing time for dynamic resource allocation is then decreased
by reducing the features using a spatial distribution–principal
component analysis (SD-PCA) technique. Self-Guided Quantum
Generative Adversarial Network with Prairie dog optimization
algorithm (SGQGAN-PDOA) is used to combine both features
and allocate resources. The workflow of this approach is given
in Figure 1.
The process starts with the task manager receiving users’
requests, wherein the IT extracts the features while being
reduced in the SD-PCA. Allocation of resources, then, utilizes
the Self-SGQGAN hyperparameters that are optimized with the
use of PDOA. Response time, waiting time, throughput, load
balancing, relative error, and reliability are considered stan-
dards for performance measurement. The research design will
ensure optimal usage of CPU, memory, and storage resources
while managing both virtualized and physical resources through
layers of virtualization. It ensures resource allocation is effi-
cient, scalable, and able to minimize interference. The objec-
tives for task scheduling efficiency and reliability will thus be
achieved.

Optimal Resource Allocation Using
Self-Guided Quantum Generative Adversarial
Network (SG-QGAN)
In this section, optimal resource allocation is carried out using
SG-QGAN [28, 29]. SG-QGAN: Optimal resource allocation
is a novel strategy that combines attention mechanisms and
quantum computing concepts to improve resource management
effectiveness.
SG module enhances the network’s emphasis on significant parts
of the input by integrating semantically learned features (SLF)
with multilevel features (MLF). Refining the features in terms of
channels and space is the main idea.
The MLF and each upsampled SLF are concatenated. After pass-
ing through multiple convolution layers, this merged feature
is subjected to Group Normalization (GN) and PReLU activa-
tion layers. This procedure produces feature maps that are more
refined and contain more significant data. The combined SLF and
MLF characteristics, represented as 𝐹∈𝑅𝐶×𝐻×𝑊, are subjected
to a spatial attention module to eliminate noise and intraclass
discrepancies brought on by small receptive fields. The key and
query feature maps are computed by the spatial attention module

Result and Discussion
This study uses a Java working platform with Cloudsim to
implement a dynamic resource allocation technique in a cloud
computing environment. The dataset includes time-series data
related to resource allocation and optimization, including request
type, quantity, priority, VM performance, resource usage metrics,
and environmental data. Demand predictions based on historical
data are also included. The experimental setup is simulated
for a virtualized cloud infrastructure involving 150 VMs using
CloudSim. Task requests from multiple users are generated and
processed to derive task-specific features, which are compressed
through SD-PCA for dimensionality reduction and enhanced
processing speed. A quantum-inspired framework, QGAN, is
applied to capture dynamic task demands and assess resource
allocation strategy efficacy. The SGQGAN encoding method
ensures a faster convergence rate and better feature mapping

Discussion
Traditional resource allocation approaches in cloud computing
suffer from numerous limitations, with most being inadequate in
effectively dealing with performance interference between VMs
and failing in accurate prediction of the resources for dynamic
workloads. Further, many of these approaches are based on tra-
ditional machine learning or heuristic algorithms that fail mis-
erably in scalability and do not readily adapt to extremely vari-
able patterns in tasks. Additionally, these approaches tend to
neglect the dimensionality of features and increase processing
times along with poor utilization of resources.

The proposed model has a few limitations that may deter
it from being used in real scenarios. First, the IT approach
in extracting features consumes much more computational
resources; hence, it delays processing time, especially when using
a resource-constrained cloud environment. In this regard, the
SD-PCA in reducing features might fail to cope with highly
dimensional data, and it loses the most important features of
the model with reduced accuracy in the allocation of resources.
Additionally, the SGQGAN-PDOA is complex since it is hybrid
and consumes so much processing power to optimize and con-
verge; hence, it is not very feasible for devices and systems that
are edge-based or have limited resources and real-time capabil-
ities. Lastly, the model is based on the principles of quantum
computing, and scalability and deployment might be problem-
atic due to current limitations in the hardware of quantum com-
puters. These factors might limit the applicability of the model
in dynamic and highly demanding cloud computing environ-
ments, especially when dealing with large user bases or real-time
resource allocation tasks.

Conclusion
The study presents a novel approach to dynamic resource
allocation in cloud computing, utilizing the SGQGAN-PDOA
algorithm. The method involves two stages: feature extrac-
tion
using
the
IT
and
feature
reduction
using
spatial
distribution–Principal
component
analysis
(SD-PCA).
The
SGQGAN-PDOA method is then used to dynamically allocate
resources. Compared to current techniques, the SGQGAN-PDOA
method requires less time to allocate resources in terms of rel-
ative error, consumption time, throughput, load balancing,
average waiting time, and response time. The system correctly
distributes resources in the cloud computing environment, with
a reliability of 80% for 150 VMs and a time consumption of
200 ms. Data mining makes resource allocation more effective
and aids in solving the resource allocation dilemma. Finding
recurring patterns in the association rules and event log is made
easier by the established resource allocation limitations.

In the future, data mining techniques will be used to improve
the suggested methodology. Also, resource allocation with
edge-cloud collaboration can be further optimized to improve
performance for latency-sensitive applications by extending
the framework. The last promising direction for extension is
enhancing security mechanisms in the proposed model to safe-
guard task data and resource allocation processes against cyber
threats.

Abstract: Cloud computing enables dynamic resource access, but efficient resource allocation remains challenging due to interference and performance limitations in virtual machine (VM) management. Efficient resource allocation in cloud computing is crucial for min- imizing interference and optimizing virtual machine (VM) performance. This study proposes a Self-Guided Quantum Generative Adversarial Network with Prairie Dog Optimization Algorithm (SGQGAN-PDOA) to reallocate tasks across VMs dynamically. The framework integrates Inception Transformer (IT) for feature extraction and Spatial Distribution–Principal Component Anal- ysis (SD-PCA) for feature reduction, enhancing processing efficiency. Implemented in Java with CloudSim, the proposed model improves resource utilization, achieving 80% reliability for 150 VMs with a 200 ms processing time. Experimental results demon- strate significant reductions in waiting time, response time, and load imbalance, outperforming existing methods. By leveraging quantum generative modeling and optimization, this approach enhances scalability, energy efficiency, and system responsiveness in dynamic cloud environments. The findings suggest that quantum-inspired scheduling frameworks offer a promising solution for adaptive and high-performance resource management in cloud computing.
